title: Common-refinement independence in reconstructed coordinates
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a normed finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a field $k$ whose characteristic is prime and different from $\ell$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$, and a specified normalized compact-support comparison family $C$ [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. Use the actual functors, maps, supplied pairs, and normalized Brown data of [def-pur-reconstructed-refinement-data]. Let $c,d$ be compactifications of $f$, and let $e,e\prime$ be two common dominating compactifications, with refinements $r:e\to c$, $s:e\to d$, $r\prime:e\prime\to c$, $s\prime:e\prime\to d$. For Brown packages $D_1,D_2,D_0,D_0\prime$ at these compactifications and an ordinary derived coefficient system $B$ of bounded-below etale origin in both dominating packages, the two actual system comparisons $\operatorname{systemCommon}(D_1,D_2,D_0,r,s,B)$ and $\operatorname{systemCommon}(D_1,D_2,D_0\prime,r\prime,s\prime,B)$ agree. Each is the ratio of the two downward refinement maps conjugated by the specified coordinate and support comparisons, inverted only on $B$. On the completed integral categories the two natural isomorphisms $\operatorname{comparison}(r)^{-1}\operatorname{comparison}(s)$ and $\operatorname{comparison}(r\prime)^{-1}\operatorname{comparison}(s\prime)$ agree (composition is read in traversal order here). No cocycle, Brown-mate or representing-pair equation is asserted.

proof.text:
take a further compactification dominating the two chosen common refinements,
and equalize the two parallel arrows to each endpoint. For intrinsic system support,
composition factors each refined downward arrow through the same further-refinement
arrow. Its component is invertible on the bounded-below etale-origin input by finite
proper/open calculus and conservative evaluations. Cancel that common factor to
identify the ratios. Coordinate conjugation cancels its intermediate beta and
coordinate counit factors, so the same equality holds for systemCommon even when
the Brown packages at the two dominating objects differ. Applying actual total limit
and restricting to complete objects gives integral commonComparison independence.
No equality is detected merely from finite evaluations.

lean.statement:
theorem reconstructedRefinementCommon :
    (∀ (c d e e' : Compactification f)
    (D₁ : At l E k C X Y f c) (D₂ : At l E k C X Y f d)
    (D₀ : At l E k C X Y f e) (D₀' : At l E k C X Y f e')
    (r : e.Refinement c) (s : e.Refinement d)
    (r' : e'.Refinement c) (s' : e'.Refinement d)
    (B : DerivedCategory (BrownTowerComparison.ProSystem X.scheme
      (integralExceptionalIntegers l E) (integralExceptionalUniformizer l E)))
    (hB : D₀.transport.siteX.Origin B) (hB' : D₀'.transport.siteX.Origin B),
    systemCommon D₁ D₂ D₀ r s B hB = systemCommon D₁ D₂ D₀' r' s' B hB') ∧
    (∀ (c d e e' : Compactification f)
    (r : e.Refinement c) (s : e.Refinement d)
    (r' : e'.Refinement c) (s' : e'.Refinement d),
    commonComparison l E k C X Y f r s = commonComparison l E k C X Y f r' s')
